skill.name: lead-scraper
skill.description: Guides AI-assisted collection of B2B lead lists by region and industry, with CSV fields for company and contact details.
skill.summary: Create structured B2B lead lists from region and industry criteria.
skill.author: Hermes-Sedimentary

security_audit.summary: The entropy finding is a false positive because SKILL.md is readable Markdown with Chinese text and front matter, not obfuscated content. I found one semantic risk: the skill targets scraping contacts, phone numbers, and addresses into lead CSV files without compliance guardrails.

remediation.suggestion: Collect only lawful public business data. Respect website terms, cite sources, and avoid personal data without consent or another valid basis.
Require user approval before browsing, scraping, exporting, or using contact details for outreach.

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (6.21 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md is plain Markdown and YAML front matter with Chinese text and one emoji, not binary, encrypted, or encoded content. The entropy heuristic appears triggered by non-ASCII content rather than obfuscation.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Contact Data Scraping
semantic_findings.description: The skill states it scrapes lead lists by region and industry into CSV fields for contact person, phone, and address. This can enable privacy-invasive collection or terms-of-service violations unless limited to lawful public business data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The stated output fields include contact names, phone numbers, and addresses for scraped leads. No visible guardrails limit collection to compliant public business data.

content.value_statement: Sales teams often need structured prospect lists by industry and location. This skill guides AI-assisted collection and CSV organization of company names, contacts, phones, and addresses.
actual_capabilities: Uses region and industry as lead search criteria.
Targets CSV fields for company name, contact person, phone, and address.
Supports sales prospecting workflows for individuals, freelancers, small businesses, and teams.
Documents compatibility with Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
Reminds users to manually verify important outputs.
limitations: No dedicated scraper code or data source list is included.
Results depend on the host AI tool and available browsing or search access.
Contact data may be stale, inaccurate, restricted, or protected by privacy laws.
Manual review is required before storage, export, or outreach.

use_cases.title: Build Local Prospect Lists
use_cases.description: Create a CSV-ready list of companies in one city and industry for compliant sales research.

use_cases.title: Research Niche Markets
use_cases.description: Collect public company details for a narrow industry segment before validating each source manually.

use_cases.title: Prepare Outreach Data
use_cases.description: Organize verified business contact fields into a consistent spreadsheet format for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Lead Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public business leads for [industry] in [region]. Include company name, public contact role, phone, address, source URL, and a verification note. Follow website terms and do not include private personal data.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CSV Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a compliant CSV lead list for [industry] in [region]. Specify the columns, acceptable public sources, exclusion rules, and manual checks needed before export.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Existing Leads
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this lead list for [industry] in [region]. Flag missing sources, stale phone numbers, duplicate companies, and entries that may include restricted personal data.

prompt_templates.title: Segment a Market
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a staged research workflow for [industry] across [regions]. Segment leads by company type, source confidence, outreach readiness, and compliance risk before producing a final CSV-ready table.

output_examples.input: Find public accounting firms in Austin for a sales prospect list.
output_examples.output: A CSV-ready table outline with company name, public phone, business address, source URL, verification status, and notes for manual review.

output_examples.input: Check this draft lead list before outreach.
output_examples.output: A review summary that identifies duplicates, missing source links, unverified phone numbers, and entries that need privacy or consent checks.

output_examples.input: Plan a lead search for solar installers in three counties.
output_examples.output: A segmented research plan with source types, search order, data fields, exclusion rules, and final CSV preparation steps.

best_practices: Use only lawful public business sources and record the source URL for each lead.
Verify phone numbers, addresses, and contact roles before exporting or outreach.
Keep collection narrow by region, industry, and legitimate business purpose.
anti_patterns: Do not scrape private personal data, gated content, or sources that prohibit automated collection.
Do not treat unverified AI output as a ready outreach list.
Do not collect broad contact lists without a clear compliance review.

faq.question: Does this skill include scraper code?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides instructions for AI-assisted lead research and CSV organization.

faq.question: What inputs does it need?
faq.answer: It is designed around a target region and industry.

faq.question: What fields can it organize?
faq.answer: It targets company name, contact person, phone, address, and CSV-ready output.

faq.question: Can it verify every lead automatically?
faq.answer: No. Users should manually verify key fields and source links.

faq.question: Is contact scraping always allowed?
faq.answer: No. Users must follow privacy laws, website terms, and consent requirements.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex as supported platforms.
